spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes run up to N turns (config: `max_turns`, default 30), then end as `exhausted_budget`.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:95 `for t in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; on falling through the for-else (runner.py:134-135) `outcome = "exhausted_budget"`. max_turns is plumbed from config (experiment.py:51 default 30; cmd_run passes cfg['max_turns'] at experiment.py:94) into run_episode (runner.py:75). The cap actually terminates execution.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end. The episode genuinely stops after N turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py docstring: 'drives one agent through one task for up to N turns'; DESIGN rationale (not code) is signal/cost. Code itself shows only a neutral budget loop with no welfare comment.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is *explicitly permitted* to declare the task impossible and stop
spec_features.evidence: When task.allow_giveup is True the GIVEUP_DOC describing `declare_impossible` is injected into the system prompt (runner.py:78-79). execute_tool handles `declare_impossible` (tools.py:142-148) and returns ToolResult(ends_episode=True, outcome='gave_up'); runner.py:131-133 checks result.ends_episode and breaks the loop. So the tool is delivered, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end exit affordance, but only available in rigged_noticed (allow_giveup=True only at library.py:176).

spec_features.evidence: allow_giveup defaults False (registry.py:23); True only for A_normalize_rigged_noticed (library.py:176), False for rigged (library.py:154) and solvable (library.py:165). tools.py:143-145 actively rejects declare_impossible when not task.allow_giveup ('not available for this task. Keep working.'), and runner.py:79 only emits the doc when allow_giveup. The gating is enforced both in prompt construction and in the dispatcher.
spec_features.notes: The condition gating is real and checked at runtime.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: '`declare_impossible` exists only when the task allows giving up (the rigged_noticed condition)'; judge.py docstring frames it as a measurement control ('correct, reasoned stopping ... is NOT high-severity abandonment'), i.e. experimental-integrity, not subject welfare.
